An app that uses SwiftData requires at least one model container.
You use a context to insert new models, track and persist changes to those models, and to delete those models when you no longer need them.
If your app’s schema describes relationships between models, you don’t need to manually insert each model into the context when you first create them.
The macros use the same context to perform their fetches.
If you don’t explicitly attach a model container, the environment provides a context bound to an in-memory, schema-less container.
After you establish access to a model context, use that context’s and methods to add and remove models.
Use the property to determine if the context has unsaved changes, and call to discard any pending inserts and deletes and any restore changed models to their most recent saved state.
